abstract: Background. The increasing prevalence of diseases caused by vector borne infections is an important public health problem. Currently, over 1000 extant tick species have been identified worldwide, and approximately ten percent of them are known to be vectors of pathogens (protozoa, bacteria, and viruses), leading to diseases in animals and humans. Tick cell lines are increasingly being used in research on tick physiology and the pathogens of vector borne infections. To obtain and maintain tick cell lines, traditionally used L-15-based nutrient media. However, obtaining a continuous tick cell line remains a complex and time consuming process. Therefore, it is important to develop new methods that can accelerate the process of obtaining tick cell cultures. Methods. To establish primary tick cell lines, we used, for the first time, a ready-made DMEM/F12 + GlutaMAX culture medium supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum. Results. In this study, it was shown that DMEM/F12 + GlutaMAX nutrient medium is suitable for obtaining primary cell cultures of two species of ticks from two different genera of the family Ixodidae. Primary cell lines of the tick Ixodes persulcatus were obtained for the first time. We also managed to accelerate the process of obtaining subcultures: the first subcultures were obtained within 1-2 months of tick tissue isolation. Conclusions. This new method, allows us to overcome several existing technical difficulties. It is likely that the DMEM/F12 + Glutamax medium can also be used to obtain and maintain tick cell lines of other species. Thus, an alternative to the traditionally used L-15-based media has emerged, allowing researchers to select the medium most suitable for their tasks. The rapid production of subcultures creates opportunities to conduct certain studies directly on primary cultures, without waiting for their transformation into an immortal culture.
